Definition: of obscure affinity; to prop, i.e. (reflexively) get fast:--stick fast.
BiblicalUsage: ereídō is the word for to prop. It occurs just once, in Acts.
TheologicalSignificance: I take ereídō as it stands — to prop — and read the passage with that plain sense in mind.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
